title: 3D chip stacking thermal density limits
bottleneck: Stacking logic dies vertically traps heat: middle and bottom dies must push watts through multiple silicon layers and bonding interfaces, with local hotspots exceeding 500 W/cm2 in advanced chiplet designs. Conventional air cooling tops out around 300 W for 2.5D stacks, forcing liquid or hybrid cooling for 3D stacks near 350 W and above. Thermal crosstalk between stacked dies also makes temperature fields unpredictable.
why_it_blocks: Thermal density, not transistor density, now caps 3D integration: dies must be power-throttled to survive, erasing the performance gains stacking was meant to deliver. Data-center operators face a cooling-cost spiral as AI packages push past air-cooling limits.
current_state: Microchannel liquid cooling, immersion, and advanced TIMs are deployed in flagship AI systems, and thermal-feasibility modeling frameworks are maturing. But 3D logic-on-logic stacks at high power remain thermally constrained in production.
